title: Module 5 quiz — WebSphere Network Deployment
description: Eight questions on BayPayCell, clusters, JNDI, pools, sessions, and operations. Synthetic names only. A live ND cell is not required.

questions.prompt: dmgr-east is down. Pay1, Pay2, and Pay3 were already started. What still works for Avery Chen’s POST /payment?
choices: Nothing: the payment ear only runs inside the deployment manager
HTTP to PaymentCluster members that are already up; new cell-wide config changes will not distribute
Only JNDI lookups, because jdbc/baypay lives exclusively on dmgr-east
Only RefundCluster, because PaymentCluster cannot run without the console
questions.explanation: The deployment manager is the admin plane. Cluster members already running continue to serve. Synchronization and new installs wait for dmgr-east. Payments do not flow through the DMGR JVM.

questions.prompt: nodeagent-pay-2 is stopped. What is the immediate operational consequence?
choices: Pay2 and Pay3 are guaranteed stopped, because they are threads inside the node agent
The entire BayPayCell stops, including IHS
Pay2 and Pay3 may still serve, but node-pay-2 will not receive configuration sync from dmgr-east
jdbc/baypay disappears from every node
questions.explanation: The node agent replicates configuration and lifecycle commands. Application servers are separate JVMs. A down nodeagent is a management-plane outage on that node, not automatic payment-process death.

questions.prompt: Why is a single cell-scoped jdbc/baypay DataSource a modernization smell on BayPayCell?
choices: JNDI cannot bind a DataSource
Payment, refund, and any reporting ear on the same bind share one pool and one failure domain
PostgreSQL forbids more than one JNDI name
Liberty cannot look up JNDI at all
questions.explanation: Cell-wide binds are convenient and couple unrelated workloads. A reporting job can exhaust the 50-connection pool that payment creates need. Isolate jdbc/baypay-payment and jdbc/baypay-refund on the way to Liberty.

questions.prompt: IHS marks Pay2 up because a TCP connect to the HTTP port succeeds, but merchants still hang on that member. What have you proven so far?
choices: Postgres is down
The plugin’s liveness check is not the same as ‘the JVM can complete a payment’
dmgr-east must be recycled first
You must enable HttpSession replication immediately
questions.explanation: TCP-up means a socket accepted. It does not mean web-container threads are free or jdbc/baypay connections are valid. Treat plugin health as a signal, not as application readiness.

questions.prompt: A developer wants HttpSession on payment.ear so Avery Chen’s cart survives a Pay1 recycle. What should you say?
choices: Required: enable memory-to-memory session replication on PaymentCluster
Required: sticky sessions at ihs-east are the payment consistency model
Reject it: payment state is Idempotency-Key plus database rows; sessions force affinity or replication
Sessions only work on Liberty, so wait for Module 6
questions.explanation: The payment API is stateless. Money lives in tables. Sessions add sticky routing and replication cost without making a retry safe. That is a Module 4 and 5 constant.

questions.prompt: Morgan Hale installs payment.ear 4.12 on PaymentCluster. What must be true before you call the rollout complete?
choices: The admin console shows the application as Installed on the cell, even if one nodeagent was down
Every intended member reports the same edition and the node sync finished on node-pay-1 and node-pay-2
dmgr-east was restarted twice
IHS was stopped for the entire window
questions.explanation: Cell install is not cluster distribution. A nodeagent outage during sync leaves mixed editions (the INCIDENT-504 class of symptom). Confirm edition on Pay1, Pay2, and Pay3.

questions.prompt: A staff engineer proposes a new FX quote service as another ear on PaymentCluster because jdbc/baypay is already there. What is the course default?
choices: Approve: reuse the cell; traditional ND is the 2026 greenfield standard
Approve only if the ear uses XA
Reject as default: do not grow the source estate; use Boot or Liberty with its own pool and config
Approve if LTPA is enabled
questions.explanation: BayPayCell is documented so you can operate and shrink it. Sharing the payment pool and class-loader policy is not a reason to add a service. Greenfield is Spring Boot or Liberty.

questions.prompt: PMI on PaymentCluster shows the WAS JDBC pool at 50/50 and web-container threads waiting. Database CPU is 18%. What is established?
choices: The database process is down
This cluster’s pool is exhausted; the cause (leak, shared reporting, hung checkout) is not yet proven
You must set maxConnections to 500
The IHS plugin certificate expired
questions.explanation: 50/50 plus waiters is exhaustion — a symptom. Low DB CPU argues against a dead PostgreSQL. Raising max is not a diagnosis. Same lesson as Module 4, different gauges (PMI vs Hikari).
